FarmoraBlogArticle1.author: By Admin
FarmoraBlogArticle1.intro: Soil is the foundation of agriculture. Healthy soil supports strong plant growth, improves crop yield and plays a vital role in maintaining a balanced ecosystem. As the demand for food continues to rise, adopting sustainable farming practices that focus on soil health has become more important than ever.
FarmoraBlogArticle1.imageAlt: Young plants growing in healthy soil

sections.heading: What is Soil Health?
sections.text: Soil health refers to the soil's ability to function as a living ecosystem. It includes a balance of nutrients, organic matter, microorganisms, and proper soil structure. Healthy soil not only supports plant growth but also helps in water retention, reduces erosion and contributes to a cleaner environment.

sections.heading: Why Soil Health Matters?
sections.text: Healthy soil leads to stronger roots, better nutrient absorption and higher crop productivity. It also reduces the need for chemical inputs, making farming more cost-effective and environmentally friendly. Additionally, well-maintained soil resists drought, supports biodiversity and ensures long-term agricultural sustainability.

FarmoraBlogArticle1.quote: “Healthy soil is not just a resource, it is a responsibility for a greener and more food-secure future.”

maintain.heading: How to Maintain Soil Health?
items: Use organic fertilizers and compost to enrich soil naturally.
Practice crop rotation to maintain nutrient balance.
Reduce chemical usage to protect soil microorganisms.
Add cover crops to prevent erosion and improve soil structure.
Adopt minimal tillage to retain soil organic matter.
Maintain proper irrigation to avoid soil degradation.
